A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E2Former-V2 research. All main-text and appendix pages are readable, including equations, figures, and tables. Relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original SPICE and OMol25 predictions, kernel and inference benchmarks, and bulk-water molecular dynamics results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds component ablations, neighbor-density experiments, OC20 results, additional kernel comparisons, and a solvated-protein simulation.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 revises the stated query/key construction: Equation (6) replaces concatenated equivariant projections with invariant inner products within each angular degree. EAAS, factorized message passing, and streaming softmax remain substantially unchanged. Appendix D presents its additional nonlinear scoring details as clarification, which alone does not establish another implementation change.

E1.justification: Appendix G adds training and evaluation on OC20 S2EF-2M, extending coverage to catalysis. Section 5.4 adds a roughly 30,000-atom solvated protein initialized from an AlphaFold prediction, extending the existing water simulation to protein structural dynamics. SPICE, OMol25, and bulk-water coverage remain.

E2.justification: The tensor-product comparison adds cuEquivariance and OpenEquivariance alongside e3nn. The inference comparison removes ORB-v3, replaces MACE-0 with MACE-OMOL, and adds EscAIP-S. Appendix J adds fully dense SDPA alongside the previously represented masked baseline. The new OC20 comparison also includes GemNet-dT, GemNet-OC, and SCN.

E3.justification: The tensor-product benchmark changes from first-/second-order plots covering 100-1,000 operations to a specified tensor product evaluated over 1,000-32,000 operations. New protocols include conservative-model component toggles at 5,000/10,000 atoms, a fixed-size neighbor-density sweep, attention-width comparisons, and a 2 ns protein trajectory evaluated by TM-score. Newly disclosed training settings do not establish changed training protocols for retained benchmarks.

E4.justification: Table 4 adds an end-to-end ablation independently enabling EAAS and Triton, testing their respective throughput and memory contributions. Appendix E tests sensitivity to neighbor density, including very sparse graphs. Appendix J examines attention-width and execution-regime effects. The protein trajectory adds structural-stability analysis beyond the retained water RDF.

E5.justification: Timing repetitions remain 10 warmups followed by 50 measurements for Figure 1 and 10 warmups followed by 10 measurements for inference throughput. The added results introduce no new seed-reporting practice, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 revises conservative SPICE aggregate energy/force MAE from 0.57/7.80 to 0.31/7.05. Table 2 changes conservative OMol25 total energy MAE from 2.09 to 1.16, while biomolecule energy MAE changes from 0.52 to 1.01. Direct inference throughput at 1,000 atoms changes from 140.0 to 58.33 steps/s. Numerous ablation, kernel, OC20, density, and protein results are added. These are reported revisions; the PDFs do not establish identical training/model configurations for attributing performance changes.

T1.justification: New Appendix B proves the existing pole-sparsity lemma using associated Legendre polynomials. Section 4.2 revises the invariant query/key definition, and Appendices D-E add operation-cost decompositions and dominance conditions. The central EAAS re-indexing derivation and Proposition 4.3 proof are retained, moving from Appendix B to C.

C1.justification: The central EAAS, fused-attention, and linear-activation-memory contributions remain. The introduction revises the stated convolution-stage speedup from approximately 6x to 1.5x and adds stable AlphaFold-protein refinement as an explicit contribution. The abstract qualifies the 20x TFLOPS claim as 'up to 20x.'

C2.justification: v2 introduces substantial qualifications: Appendix D discusses an efficiency/expressivity trade-off, Appendix E explains why an edge-centric baseline can outperform the method at very low neighbor counts, and Appendix J discusses lower achieved TFLOPS than dense SDPA in terms of irregular access and precision. Section 5.2 newly attributes the dominant end-to-end gain to Triton, with EAAS providing an additional benefit.

D1.justification: Appendix I newly documents training schedules, conservative initialization from the direct checkpoint, losses, learning rates, and backbone hyperparameters. Section 5.4 supplies GROMACS 2025.3 and NVT/300 K simulation details. The code link changes from the e2formerv2 branch to main. Conversely, the throughput appendix drops v1's explicit PBC disabling, sparse-attention override, and other configuration overrides; this is lost documentation, not evidence that those settings changed.

R1.justification: A new related-work subsection positions the method against Gaunt tensor products, tensor decomposition, expressivity/runtime research, cuEquivariance, and OpenEquivariance. Appendix D substantially expands comparisons with EquiformerV2/eSEN/eSCN through nonlinearities and computational costs. The taxonomy also changes: Allegro moves to tensor-product methods and ViSNet to scalar/vector methods. This exceeds bibliographic metadata updating.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, related work, and attention explanation undergo substantial rewriting. Experiments are reorganized to present predictive accuracy first, incorporating the former dataset subsection. The appendices are reorganized around retained material and new proof, analysis, and training sections, and an impact statement is added.

P2.justification: The original tensor-product plots are replaced by a multi-backend runtime table. New displays cover ablations, neighbor density, OC20, training configurations, and dense-attention comparisons. The water RDF becomes one panel alongside a new protein TM-score plot, and the inference table's comparator columns are redesigned. The architecture diagram and four-panel kernel benchmark are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central efficiency evidence through optimized comparison backends and component ablations, addressing important validation gaps in v1. Neighbor-density limits and the newly supplied training configuration also improve interpretability and reproducibility. These gains outweigh remaining weaknesses: the OMol25 prose still claims 1.27 energy MAE while Table 2 reports 1.16, and removal of throughput preprocessing details weakens that benchmark's documentation. The improvement rests on stronger validation and documentation, rather than the changed accuracy scores.
